name: Project 3: FastAPI service
title: Build a production-shaped tickets API with FastAPI
thesis: You will build a small support-tickets REST API with validation, a real database, API-key auth, correct status codes and tests. Almost every FDE engagement ends with some service like this that a customer's systems call, so being able to stand one up cleanly in an afternoon is core craft.

steps.title: Define the API contract with Pydantic
steps.body:
These models are the promise your API makes. TicketCreate says what a client must send, TicketUpdate makes every field optional for PATCH, and TicketOut says what comes back.

Enums for priority and status mean a typo like "urgent" is rejected with a 422 before your code ever runs. from_attributes=True lets FastAPI turn a database row straight into a response.

Also create an empty app/__init__.py so Python treats app as a package.
steps.code:
"""Pydantic v2 models: the shapes of data going in and out of the API."""
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field


class Priority(str, Enum):
    low = "low"
    medium = "medium"
    high = "high"


class Status(str, Enum):
    open = "open"
    in_progress = "in_progress"
    closed = "closed"


class TicketCreate(BaseModel):
    """What a client sends to create a ticket."""
    title: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)
    description: str = Field(default="", max_length=5000)
    priority: Priority = Priority.medium


class TicketUpdate(BaseModel):
    """Partial update: every field is optional (PATCH semantics)."""
    title: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=200)
    description: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=5000)
    priority: Priority | None = None
    status: Status | None = None


class TicketOut(BaseModel):
    """What the API returns. from_attributes lets us build it from an ORM row."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

    id: int
    title: str
    description: str
    priority: Priority
    status: Status
    created_at: datetime
    updated_at: datetime

steps.title: Set up the database with SQLAlchemy 2
steps.body:
The Ticket class maps to a tickets table using the typed Mapped[...] style from SQLAlchemy 2. updated_at refreshes itself on every update.

get_db is a dependency that opens one session per request and always closes it, even if the request fails. Tests will swap this out for an in-memory database.
steps.code:
"""Database setup with SQLAlchemy 2 (typed ORM) on SQLite."""
import os
from collections.abc import Iterator
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from sqlalchemy import String, Text, create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, Session, mapped_column, sessionmaker

DATABASE_URL = os.getenv("DATABASE_URL", "sqlite:///./tickets.db")

# check_same_thread=False: FastAPI may use a session from a different thread.
engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(bind=engine, expire_on_commit=False)


def utcnow() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc)


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


class Ticket(Base):
    __tablename__ = "tickets"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(200))
    description: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text, default="")
    priority: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(20), default="medium")
    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(20), default="open", index=True)
    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(default=utcnow)
    updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(default=utcnow, onupdate=utcnow)


def init_db() -> None:
    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)


def get_db() -> Iterator[Session]:
    """FastAPI dependency: one session per request, always closed."""
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

steps.title: Add API-key auth as a dependency
steps.body:
Writing auth as a dependency means one line (dependencies=[Depends(require_api_key)]) protects a route, and you cannot forget the check inside the handler.

A missing key returns 401 (who are you?), a wrong key returns 403 (you are not allowed). If the server has no key configured it returns 500 instead of silently letting everyone in. secrets.compare_digest avoids timing attacks.
steps.code:
"""API-key auth as a reusable FastAPI dependency."""
import os
import secrets

from fastapi import HTTPException, Security, status
from fastapi.security import APIKeyHeader

api_key_header = APIKeyHeader(name="X-API-Key", auto_error=False)


def require_api_key(key: str | None = Security(api_key_header)) -> str:
    expected = os.getenv("API_KEY")
    if not expected:
        # Fail closed: a server with no key configured should not be open to everyone.
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "API_KEY is not configured")
    if key is None:
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, "Missing X-API-Key header")
    # compare_digest avoids leaking the key through response timing.
    if not secrets.compare_digest(key, expected):
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN, "Invalid API key")
    return key

steps.title: Write the routes
steps.body:
Four endpoints, each with a deliberate status code: POST returns 201 Created, GET of a missing id returns 404, and bad input returns 422 automatically.

The PATCH handler uses model_dump(exclude_unset=True) so only fields the client actually sent are changed. Without it, omitted fields would be overwritten with None. The list endpoint supports a status filter plus limit/offset pagination with sane bounds.

steps.title: Test fixtures: an isolated database per test
steps.body:
Every test gets a brand new in-memory SQLite database via app.dependency_overrides, so tests never touch tickets.db and never affect each other. StaticPool keeps a single connection so the in-memory data survives across requests.

The TestClient is created with the API key already in its headers, which keeps each test short. Also create an empty tests/__init__.py.
steps.code:
"""Test fixtures: a fresh in-memory database and an API key for every test."""
import os

os.environ.setdefault("DATABASE_URL", "sqlite://")  # never touch tickets.db during tests

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from sqlalchemy.pool import StaticPool

from app.db import Base, get_db
from app.main import app

TEST_KEY = "test-key"


@pytest.fixture()
def client(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("API_KEY", TEST_KEY)
    # StaticPool keeps ONE connection so the in-memory DB survives across requests.
    engine = create_engine("sqlite://", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False},
                           poolclass=StaticPool)
    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
    TestSession = sessionmaker(bind=engine, expire_on_commit=False)

    def override_get_db():
        db = TestSession()
        try:
            yield db
        finally:
            db.close()

    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
    with TestClient(app, headers={"X-API-Key": TEST_KEY}) as c:
        yield c
    app.dependency_overrides.clear()

steps.title: Test the behavior, including failures
steps.body: Good API tests check the unhappy paths as carefully as the happy one: 422 on bad input, 404 on missing ids, 401 and 403 on auth, and that PATCH leaves untouched fields alone.
steps.code:
def make(client, **kw):
    body = {"title": "Printer on fire", "priority": "high", **kw}
    r = client.post("/tickets", json=body)
    assert r.status_code == 201, r.text
    return r.json()


def test_create_returns_201_and_defaults(client):
    t = make(client)
    assert t["id"] == 1
    assert t["status"] == "open"
    assert t["description"] == ""


def test_validation_error_is_422(client):
    assert client.post("/tickets", json={"title": ""}).status_code == 422
    assert client.post("/tickets", json={"title": "x", "priority": "urgent"}).status_code == 422


def test_get_and_404(client):
    t = make(client)
    assert client.get(f"/tickets/{t['id']}").json()["title"] == "Printer on fire"
    assert client.get("/tickets/999").status_code == 404


def test_list_with_filter_and_pagination(client):
    for i in range(3):
        make(client, title=f"t{i}")
    client.patch("/tickets/2", json={"status": "closed"})
    assert len(client.get("/tickets").json()) == 3
    closed = client.get("/tickets", params={"status": "closed"}).json()
    assert [t["id"] for t in closed] == [2]
    page = client.get("/tickets", params={"limit": 1, "offset": 1}).json()
    assert [t["id"] for t in page] == [2]


def test_patch_updates_only_sent_fields(client):
    t = make(client, description="smoke")
    r = client.patch(f"/tickets/{t['id']}", json={"status": "in_progress"})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert body["status"] == "in_progress"
    assert body["description"] == "smoke"   # untouched
    assert client.patch("/tickets/42", json={"status": "closed"}).status_code == 404
    assert client.patch(f"/tickets/{t['id']}", json={"title": None}).status_code == 422


def test_auth_missing_and_wrong_key(client):
    assert client.get("/tickets", headers={"X-API-Key": "nope"}).status_code == 403
    client.headers.pop("X-API-Key")
    assert client.get("/tickets").status_code == 401

project.interview: I built a small tickets API in FastAPI with Pydantic v2 contracts, SQLAlchemy 2 on SQLite and an API-key dependency, and tested it with TestClient against an in-memory database via dependency overrides. The trade-offs I would call out: API keys are simple but not per-user, so a real deployment would move to OAuth or signed tokens; SQLite is fine for one process but I kept the database behind a URL so swapping to Postgres is a config change; and I chose PATCH with exclude_unset so partial updates never wipe fields.

ideas: Pydantic models are your API contract: bad input is rejected with 422 before your code runs.
Status codes are part of the interface: 201 for create, 404 for missing, 401 for no credentials, 403 for wrong credentials.
Dependencies (get_db, require_api_key) keep cross-cutting concerns out of handlers and make them easy to override in tests.
Each test should get its own fresh database so tests are fast, isolated and repeatable.
traps: Using model_dump() instead of model_dump(exclude_unset=True) in PATCH, which overwrites omitted fields with None.
Defaulting to an open server when API_KEY is not set; always fail closed.
Letting tests write to the real database file, so results depend on leftover data from earlier runs.
qa: Why return 401 for a missing key but 403 for a wrong one?

401 means the request is not authenticated at all, so the client should supply credentials. 403 means credentials were supplied and understood but are not allowed. The distinction helps client developers debug: one says add a header, the other says your key is wrong or lacks access.
How do your tests avoid touching the real database?

The app gets its session through a get_db dependency. In tests I use app.dependency_overrides to swap it for a session bound to an in-memory SQLite engine with StaticPool, created fresh per test. So every test starts empty and nothing leaks between tests or onto disk.

name: Project 4: ingestion
title: Ingest from a flaky paginated API without losing or duplicating data
thesis: You will build a client that pulls customers from a misbehaving paginated API, retries sensibly, quarantines bad rows and resumes after a crash. Customer data sources are always messier than the docs say, and FDEs are trusted when their pipelines survive rate limits, outages and dirty data.

steps.title: Dependencies
steps.body: Only three packages: Pydantic for validation, tenacity for retries, pytest for tests. SQLite comes with Python, and there is no network or API key involved, because the API is a local mock. Create empty ingest/__init__.py and tests/__init__.py files too.

steps.title: Build a misbehaving mock API
steps.body:
The mock acts like an HTTP endpoint: get_page(cursor) returns a status code, a JSON body and headers. You can script failures (for example [429, 500]) that it returns before behaving, which makes retry tests deterministic.

It also generates 25 customers with a fixed seed, and breaks every sixth row in a different way: a bad email, a missing name, an impossible date, an unknown plan. Cursors are base64 so clients treat them as opaque, just like real APIs.

steps.title: Define what a valid row looks like
steps.body:
The Customer model is the contract. Anything that fails it goes to the dead-letter table instead of crashing the job or silently landing bad data.

extra="ignore" means new fields the API adds later will not break you, and str_strip_whitespace cleans up stray spaces.
steps.code:
"""The contract for a valid customer row. Anything that fails goes to the dead-letter table."""
from datetime import date
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field


class Customer(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="ignore", str_strip_whitespace=True)

    id: int = Field(gt=0)
    name: str = Field(min_length=1)
    email: str = Field(pattern=r"^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$")
    plan: Literal["free", "pro", "enterprise"]
    signup_date: date

steps.title: Store rows, dead letters and the checkpoint atomically
steps.body:
Three tables: customers for good rows, dead_letter for bad rows plus the reason and the page they came from, and checkpoint for the next cursor.

The key design choice is in save_page: one page's rows and the new cursor are committed in a single transaction. If the process dies mid-page, nothing from that page is saved and the checkpoint still points at it, so the rerun redoes exactly that page. The upsert (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE) makes replays idempotent, so re-ingesting a row never creates a duplicate.

steps.title: The client: retry, validate, store, repeat
steps.body:
fetch_page wraps each call in a tenacity Retrying loop. It only retries 429 and 5xx, because a 400 or 404 will fail the same way every time. The wait grows exponentially (0.5s, 1s, 2s...) with random jitter so many clients do not hammer the API in lockstep, and it gives up after max_attempts.

run_ingestion starts from the saved checkpoint, validates each row, writes the page, and follows next_cursor until it is null. The wait strategy is a parameter so tests can run without sleeping.

steps.title: A command-line entry point
steps.body: run.py wires the pieces together with logging so you can watch the retries happen. The --fail flag controls which errors the mock throws first.
steps.code:
"""Run the ingestion against the flaky mock API and print a summary.

Usage: python run.py [--db ingest.db] [--fail 429,500,500]
"""
import argparse
import logging

from ingest.client import run_ingestion
from ingest.mock_api import MockCustomerAPI
from ingest.store import Store

if __name__ == "__main__":
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--db", default="ingest.db")
    p.add_argument("--fail", default="429,500", help="status codes the mock returns first")
    args = p.parse_args()
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

    failures = [int(x) for x in args.fail.split(",") if x]
    api = MockCustomerAPI(failures=failures)
    store = Store(args.db)
    stats = run_ingestion(api, store)
    print(f"run: {stats} | API calls: {api.calls}")
    print(f"table totals: customers={store.count('customers')} "
          f"dead_letter={store.count('dead_letter')}")
    for raw, err in store.conn.execute("SELECT raw, error FROM dead_letter LIMIT 3"):
        print("  DLQ:", err, "<-", raw[:60])

steps.title: Test every failure mode
steps.body:
The tests cover the happy path, the dead-letter reasons, retrying through 429/500/503, giving up after max attempts, never retrying a 400, and the most important one: an outage after page 1, followed by a rerun that resumes at row 11 with no duplicates and then becomes a no-op.

Passing wait=wait_none() keeps the whole suite under a second.
steps.code:
import pytest
from tenacity import wait_none

from ingest.client import PermanentHTTPError, RetryableHTTPError, run_ingestion
from ingest.mock_api import MockCustomerAPI, decode_cursor, make_customers
from ingest.store import Store

FAST = wait_none()  # no sleeping in tests


@pytest.fixture()
def store(tmp_path):
    return Store(str(tmp_path / "t.db"))


def test_happy_path_splits_good_and_bad(store):
    stats = run_ingestion(MockCustomerAPI(), store, wait=FAST)
    assert stats == {"pages": 3, "good": 21, "bad": 4}   # rows 6, 12, 18, 24 are broken
    assert store.count("customers") == 21
    assert store.count("dead_letter") == 4
    assert store.load_checkpoint() == (None, True)


def test_dead_letter_keeps_raw_row_and_reason(store):
    run_ingestion(MockCustomerAPI(), store, wait=FAST)
    errors = [e for (e,) in store.conn.execute("SELECT error FROM dead_letter ORDER BY id")]
    assert "email" in errors[0] and "name" in errors[1]
    assert "signup_date" in errors[2] and "plan" in errors[3]


def test_retries_through_429_and_500(store):
    api = MockCustomerAPI(failures=[429, 500, 503])
    stats = run_ingestion(api, store, wait=FAST)
    assert stats["good"] == 21
    assert api.calls == 3 + 3   # three failures, then three pages


def test_gives_up_after_max_attempts(store):
    api = MockCustomerAPI(failures=[500] * 10)
    with pytest.raises(RetryableHTTPError):
        run_ingestion(api, store, max_attempts=4, wait=FAST)
    assert api.calls == 4


def test_4xx_is_not_retried(store):
    api = MockCustomerAPI(failures=[400])
    with pytest.raises(PermanentHTTPError):
        run_ingestion(api, store, wait=FAST)
    assert api.calls == 1


class DiesAfterFirstPage(MockCustomerAPI):
    """Serves page 1, then returns 500 forever (an outage mid-run)."""
    def get_page(self, cursor=None):
        if self.calls >= 1:
            self.calls += 1
            return 500, {}, {}
        return super().get_page(cursor)


def test_resumes_from_checkpoint_without_duplicates(store):
    api = DiesAfterFirstPage()
    with pytest.raises(RetryableHTTPError):
        run_ingestion(api, store, max_attempts=3, wait=FAST)
    cursor, done = store.load_checkpoint()
    assert decode_cursor(cursor) == 10 and not done
    assert store.count("customers") == 9   # page 1 had 10 rows, 1 bad

    # Second run with a healthy API picks up at row 11, not row 1.
    api2 = MockCustomerAPI()
    stats = run_ingestion(api2, store, wait=FAST)
    assert stats["pages"] == 2 and api2.calls == 2
    assert store.count("customers") == 21
    # A third run is a no-op because the job is marked done.
    assert run_ingestion(MockCustomerAPI(), store, wait=FAST)["pages"] == 0


def test_mock_data_is_deterministic():
    assert make_customers() == make_customers()

stretch: Honor the Retry-After header on 429 responses instead of the computed backoff.
Wrap the mock in a tiny FastAPI app and call it with httpx, adding connect and read timeouts.
Add reprocess_dead_letters() that re-validates DLQ rows after you fix a validation rule.
Log metrics (rows per second, retries, DLQ rate) and fail the run if the DLQ rate goes above 5%.
project.interview: I built an ingestion client for a paginated API that retries 429 and 5xx with exponential backoff and jitter via tenacity, validates rows with Pydantic, sends bad rows to a dead-letter table with the reason, and checkpoints the cursor in the same transaction as the page's writes. Trade-offs I'd mention: committing per page means a crash can replay at most one page, which is safe only because writes are upserts; I don't retry 4xx because they are deterministic; and a dead-letter table keeps the pipeline moving but needs someone to own reviewing it, or it becomes a silent data loss bucket.

ideas: Retry only what can succeed on retry: 429 and 5xx yes, 4xx no.
Exponential backoff with jitter protects the API you are calling and avoids synchronized retry storms.
Commit the checkpoint in the same transaction as the data it covers, and make writes idempotent, so crashes are safe to resume.
Quarantine bad rows with the reason instead of failing the whole job or dropping them silently.
traps: Saving the cursor before (or separately from) the rows, so a crash skips data or replays it into duplicates.
Retrying forever or retrying 400s, which wastes time and can get you rate-limited harder.
Actually sleeping in tests, making the suite slow and flaky; inject the wait strategy instead.
qa: Why add jitter to exponential backoff?

Without jitter, every client that failed at the same moment retries at the same moment, so the API gets hit by synchronized waves and may keep failing. Random jitter spreads retries out in time, which gives the server room to recover and raises the success rate for everyone.
What happens if your job crashes halfway through page 2?

Page 2's rows and the checkpoint update are in one SQLite transaction, so nothing from page 2 is committed and the checkpoint still points at page 2. On rerun the job fetches page 2 again. Because writes are upserts keyed on customer id, even a replay of an already-saved page would not create duplicates.

setup.body: A virtual environment keeps this project's packages separate from everything else on your machine.
setup.code:
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt

setup.title: Virtual environment (Windows PowerShell)
setup.body: Same thing on Windows. If activation is blocked, run Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned once.

setup.title: Copy the Project 3 code
setup.body: Copy the app/ and tests/ folders and .env.example from Project 3 into this folder so it stands alone. The only code change is in app/main.py (step 2).

setup.title: Optional tools for containers
setup.body: Tests do not need any of these. To build and deploy, install Docker Desktop (Windows/macOS) or Docker Engine (Linux), then kind and kubectl. Check they work.

steps.title: Split runtime and dev dependencies
steps.body: The image only needs what the app uses at runtime. Test tools live in requirements-dev.txt, which includes the runtime file with -r. Smaller images build faster, pull faster and have fewer packages to patch.

steps.title: Add liveness and readiness endpoints
steps.body:
/healthz answers "is the process alive?" and deliberately does not touch the database. If it did, a slow database would make Kubernetes restart perfectly healthy pods, which makes an outage worse.

/readyz answers "can I serve traffic right now?" by running SELECT 1. When it fails, Kubernetes stops sending traffic to that pod but does not kill it. Neither endpoint needs the API key, because the platform calls them.

steps.title: The unchanged Project 3 modules
steps.body: These are copied as-is from Project 3 (plus an empty app/__init__.py and tests/__init__.py). The database URL comes from DATABASE_URL, which is what lets the container point it at a mounted volume.
steps.code:
# ===== app/schemas.py =====
"""Pydantic v2 models: the shapes of data going in and out of the API."""
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field


class Priority(str, Enum):
    low = "low"
    medium = "medium"
    high = "high"


class Status(str, Enum):
    open = "open"
    in_progress = "in_progress"
    closed = "closed"


class TicketCreate(BaseModel):
    """What a client sends to create a ticket."""
    title: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)
    description: str = Field(default="", max_length=5000)
    priority: Priority = Priority.medium


class TicketUpdate(BaseModel):
    """Partial update: every field is optional (PATCH semantics)."""
    title: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=200)
    description: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=5000)
    priority: Priority | None = None
    status: Status | None = None


class TicketOut(BaseModel):
    """What the API returns. from_attributes lets us build it from an ORM row."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

    id: int
    title: str
    description: str
    priority: Priority
    status: Status
    created_at: datetime
    updated_at: datetime

# ===== app/db.py =====
"""Database setup with SQLAlchemy 2 (typed ORM) on SQLite."""
import os
from collections.abc import Iterator
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from sqlalchemy import String, Text, create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, Session, mapped_column, sessionmaker

DATABASE_URL = os.getenv("DATABASE_URL", "sqlite:///./tickets.db")

# check_same_thread=False: FastAPI may use a session from a different thread.
engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(bind=engine, expire_on_commit=False)


def utcnow() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc)


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


class Ticket(Base):
    __tablename__ = "tickets"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(200))
    description: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text, default="")
    priority: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(20), default="medium")
    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(20), default="open", index=True)
    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(default=utcnow)
    updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(default=utcnow, onupdate=utcnow)


def init_db() -> None:
    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)


def get_db() -> Iterator[Session]:
    """FastAPI dependency: one session per request, always closed."""
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

# ===== app/auth.py =====
"""API-key auth as a reusable FastAPI dependency."""
import os
import secrets

from fastapi import HTTPException, Security, status
from fastapi.security import APIKeyHeader

api_key_header = APIKeyHeader(name="X-API-Key", auto_error=False)


def require_api_key(key: str | None = Security(api_key_header)) -> str:
    expected = os.getenv("API_KEY")
    if not expected:
        # Fail closed: a server with no key configured should not be open to everyone.
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "API_KEY is not configured")
    if key is None:
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, "Missing X-API-Key header")
    # compare_digest avoids leaking the key through response timing.
    if not secrets.compare_digest(key, expected):
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN, "Invalid API key")
    return key

# ===== tests/conftest.py =====
"""Test fixtures: a fresh in-memory database and an API key for every test."""
import os

os.environ.setdefault("DATABASE_URL", "sqlite://")  # never touch tickets.db during tests

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from sqlalchemy.pool import StaticPool

from app.db import Base, get_db
from app.main import app

TEST_KEY = "test-key"


@pytest.fixture()
def client(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("API_KEY", TEST_KEY)
    # StaticPool keeps ONE connection so the in-memory DB survives across requests.
    engine = create_engine("sqlite://", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False},
                           poolclass=StaticPool)
    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
    TestSession = sessionmaker(bind=engine, expire_on_commit=False)

    def override_get_db():
        db = TestSession()
        try:
            yield db
        finally:
            db.close()

    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
    with TestClient(app, headers={"X-API-Key": TEST_KEY}) as c:
        yield c
    app.dependency_overrides.clear()

# ===== tests/test_tickets.py =====
def make(client, **kw):
    body = {"title": "Printer on fire", "priority": "high", **kw}
    r = client.post("/tickets", json=body)
    assert r.status_code == 201, r.text
    return r.json()


def test_create_returns_201_and_defaults(client):
    t = make(client)
    assert t["id"] == 1
    assert t["status"] == "open"
    assert t["description"] == ""


def test_validation_error_is_422(client):
    assert client.post("/tickets", json={"title": ""}).status_code == 422
    assert client.post("/tickets", json={"title": "x", "priority": "urgent"}).status_code == 422


def test_get_and_404(client):
    t = make(client)
    assert client.get(f"/tickets/{t['id']}").json()["title"] == "Printer on fire"
    assert client.get("/tickets/999").status_code == 404


def test_list_with_filter_and_pagination(client):
    for i in range(3):
        make(client, title=f"t{i}")
    client.patch("/tickets/2", json={"status": "closed"})
    assert len(client.get("/tickets").json()) == 3
    closed = client.get("/tickets", params={"status": "closed"}).json()
    assert [t["id"] for t in closed] == [2]
    page = client.get("/tickets", params={"limit": 1, "offset": 1}).json()
    assert [t["id"] for t in page] == [2]


def test_patch_updates_only_sent_fields(client):
    t = make(client, description="smoke")
    r = client.patch(f"/tickets/{t['id']}", json={"status": "in_progress"})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert body["status"] == "in_progress"
    assert body["description"] == "smoke"   # untouched
    assert client.patch("/tickets/42", json={"status": "closed"}).status_code == 404
    assert client.patch(f"/tickets/{t['id']}", json={"title": None}).status_code == 422


def test_auth_missing_and_wrong_key(client):
    assert client.get("/tickets", headers={"X-API-Key": "nope"}).status_code == 403
    client.headers.pop("X-API-Key")
    assert client.get("/tickets").status_code == 401

steps.title: Test the health endpoints
steps.body: Three new tests: /healthz works without a key, /readyz reports ready, and /readyz returns 503 when the database session is broken. The last one uses a dependency override with a fake session that raises, so you can test an outage without an outage.

steps.title: A multi-stage Dockerfile
steps.body:
Stage 1 (builder) creates a virtual environment and installs dependencies. Stage 2 (runtime) copies only that venv and the app code, so pip caches and build leftovers never ship.

requirements.txt is copied before the code, so Docker reuses the cached dependency layer until dependencies actually change. The container runs as a non-root user, stores SQLite in /data, and has a HEALTHCHECK so docker ps shows healthy or unhealthy. .dockerignore keeps venvs, databases, secrets and tests out of the build context.
steps.code:
# ---- Stage 1: build. Has pip and build tools; its leftovers never ship. ----
FROM python:3.12-slim AS builder
WORKDIR /build
RUN python -m venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"
# Copy requirements first so this layer is cached until dependencies change.
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# ---- Stage 2: runtime. Only the venv and our code. ----
FROM python:3.12-slim AS runtime
ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH" \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    DATABASE_URL=sqlite:////data/tickets.db
# Run as a non-root user.
RUN useradd --create-home --uid 10001 app && mkdir /data && chown app /data
COPY --from=builder /opt/venv /opt/venv
WORKDIR /srv
COPY app ./app
USER app
EXPOSE 8000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
  CMD python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/healthz', timeout=2)"
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

# ----- .dockerignore -----
.venv
__pycache__
.pytest_cache
*.db
.env
.git
tests
k8s
.github

steps.title: docker compose for local runs
steps.body: Compose records how to run the container: port mapping, environment and a named volume so tickets survive restarts. API_KEY is read from your shell or a .env file, with a dev default, so no secret is committed.
steps.code:
services:
  api:
    build: .
    image: tickets-api:local
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    environment:
      API_KEY: ${API_KEY:-change-me-dev-key}   # read from your shell or a .env file
      DATABASE_URL: sqlite:////data/tickets.db
    volumes:
      - tickets-data:/data                     # keeps the SQLite file across restarts
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  tickets-data:

steps.title: CI with GitHub Actions
steps.body: On every push and pull request, the test job runs pytest on Python 3.11 and 3.12. Only if that passes does the docker job build the image and smoke-test it: start the container, wait for /readyz, then make an authenticated request. A broken Dockerfile is caught before anyone deploys it.
steps.code:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
          cache: pip
      - run: pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
      - run: pytest -q

  docker:
    needs: test            # only build the image if tests pass
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: docker build -t tickets-api:${{ github.sha }} .
      - name: Smoke test the container
        run: |
          docker run -d --name api -p 8000:8000 -e API_KEY=ci-key tickets-api:${{ github.sha }}
          for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -fs localhost:8000/readyz && break; sleep 1; done
          curl -fs -H "X-API-Key: ci-key" localhost:8000/tickets

steps.title: Kubernetes manifests
steps.body:
The Deployment runs the image with the API key pulled from a Secret, a readiness probe on /readyz, a liveness probe on /healthz, and resource requests and limits. imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent tells it to use the image you loaded into kind.

Because SQLite lives in the pod, it runs one replica with an emptyDir volume (data is lost when the pod is replaced). Scaling out needs an external database such as Postgres. The Service gives the pods a stable name and port inside the cluster.
steps.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tickets-api
  labels: {app: tickets-api}
spec:
  # SQLite lives inside the pod, so keep ONE replica. Use Postgres before scaling out.
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app: tickets-api}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app: tickets-api}
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: api
          image: tickets-api:local
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent     # use the image loaded into kind, don't pull
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8000
          env:
            - name: API_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef: {name: tickets-api, key: api-key}
            - name: DATABASE_URL
              value: sqlite:////data/tickets.db
          volumeMounts:
            - {name: data, mountPath: /data}
          readinessProbe:                   # gate traffic until the DB answers
            httpGet: {path: /readyz, port: 8000}
            initialDelaySeconds: 2
            periodSeconds: 5
          livenessProbe:                    # restart only if the process is stuck
            httpGet: {path: /healthz, port: 8000}
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 50m, memory: 64Mi}
            limits: {cpu: 500m, memory: 256Mi}
      volumes:
        - name: data
          emptyDir: {}                      # demo only: data is lost when the pod is replaced
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: tickets-api
spec:
  selector: {app: tickets-api}
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8000

run.code:
# 1. Plain Python
export API_KEY=dev-key && uvicorn app.main:app --reload
curl localhost:8000/healthz        # {"status":"ok"}

# 2. Docker
docker build -t tickets-api:local .
docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 -e API_KEY=dev-key tickets-api:local
curl localhost:8000/readyz         # {"status":"ready"}
docker ps                          # STATUS: Up 20 seconds (healthy)

# 3. docker compose (data persists in a named volume)
API_KEY=dev-key docker compose up --build
docker compose down -v

# 4. Kubernetes on kind
kind create cluster --name tickets
kind load docker-image tickets-api:local --name tickets
kubectl create secret generic tickets-api --from-literal=api-key=dev-key
kubectl apply -f k8s/
kubectl rollout status deployment/tickets-api
kubectl port-forward service/tickets-api 8080:80
curl -H "X-API-Key: dev-key" localhost:8080/tickets    # []
kind delete cluster --name tickets

pytest -q
# .........                                [100%]
# 9 passed in 0.7s
# No Docker needed: tests use TestClient and an in-memory SQLite database.

Push the image to GitHub Container Registry from CI when you create a git tag.
Add a HorizontalPodAutoscaler and load-test it with a simple script.

project.interview: I containerized a FastAPI service with a multi-stage, non-root Docker image, added separate liveness and readiness endpoints, wired GitHub Actions to test and then build and smoke-test the image, and deployed it to a local kind cluster with probes, resource limits and the API key in a Secret. The trade-offs I would raise: liveness must not depend on the database or you get restart storms; SQLite forces a single replica, so real scale means an external database; and kind proves the manifests work but not cloud specifics like load balancers, IAM or persistent volumes.

ideas: Liveness asks if the process should be restarted; readiness asks if it should get traffic. They check different things.
Multi-stage builds ship only what runs, which makes images smaller, faster and safer.
CI should run tests first and then prove the built image actually starts and answers requests.
Secrets come from the environment (compose env, Kubernetes Secret), never from the image or the repo.
traps: Pointing the liveness probe at a check that depends on the database, so a DB blip restarts every pod.
Copying the whole folder before installing dependencies, which busts the Docker layer cache on every code change.
Forgetting kind load docker-image, so Kubernetes tries to pull tickets-api:local from a registry and the pod sits in ErrImagePull.
qa: What is the difference between a readiness and a liveness probe, and what does each check here?

Readiness decides whether a pod receives traffic; failing it removes the pod from the Service without killing it. Liveness decides whether the container is stuck and must be restarted. Here readiness hits /readyz, which runs SELECT 1 against the database, and liveness hits /healthz, which only confirms the process answers HTTP, so a slow database stops traffic but does not trigger restarts.
Why use a multi-stage Dockerfile for a Python app?

The builder stage has pip and any build tools and produces a virtual environment. The runtime stage copies only that venv and the app code, so caches, compilers and build files never ship. You get a smaller image, faster pulls, and less attack surface, and copying requirements.txt first keeps the dependency layer cached between code changes.
